rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry is called al-sākhkha because its intensity deafens ears to everything else, making people hear only it; the metaphor conveys the calamity’s force.
rows.anchor: şiddetinden dolayı kendisinden başkasını işittirmeyecek vechile kulağı sağır etmesidir

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-sahh means listening closely; the cry is called al-sākhkha metaphorically because people listen to it, with the listener attributed to the cry for emphasis.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf demiştir ki: “‘Sahh’ isâha etmek, yani iyice kulak verip dinlemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both explanations stress severity; the author says the explanation based on deafening others is closer in this context, while the other stresses being heard.
rows.anchor: öbürüsünde de başkasından sağır edecek vechile dinletmesi haysiyetlerine ziyade tenbih vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list moves upward through degrees of kinship and love, showing that a person will flee even from the closest and dearest relatives on that day.
rows.anchor: biraderden başlayarak yakınlık ve mahabbetin derecâtına göre firarda bir terakki üslûbu vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person is absorbed by an overwhelming personal concern; some flee to focus on themselves, while others fear relatives’ claims for wrongs done to them.
rows.anchor: kendisini meşgul eden öyle mühim bir işi, bir şuğlü vardır ki başından aşar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Relatives may demand an account: a brother for lack of help, parents for neglect, a wife for unlawful provision, and children for failure to teach religion.
rows.anchor: kardeş “sen bana dünyada yardım etmedin” diye, ana baba “sen bize iyilikte kusur ettin” diye

rows.speaker: Sevde binti Zem‘a
rows.claim: She reports that people will be resurrected barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and overwhelmed by sweat; when she fears they will see one another’s shame, the Prophet says they will be too occupied and recites this verse.
rows.anchor: Ümmü’l-mü’minîn Sevde binti Zem‘a radıyallahu anhâ’dan rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: A person will be especially weary of seeing someone familiar because he fears that person will demand redress for an injustice he committed.
rows.anchor: Ebû Ubeyde’nin ve İbn Münzir’in Katâde’den rivayetlerinde de: Kıyamet günü insan tanıdığı bir kimseyi görmekten sıkıldığı kadar hiçbir şeyden sıkılmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radiant faces shine like morning; in this passage they signify the effects of reverence for God, faith, Islam, obedience, and purification.
rows.anchor: Allah saygısı ve iman ve islâm ile Allah’ın emirlerini edâ ederek tezekkînin eseridir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: He explains the brightness as resulting from night worship; the author cites a report that plentiful night prayer beautifies the face by day.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayette “kıyâm-ı leyldendir” denilmiş, çünkü bir hadîste

rows.speaker: Dahhâk
rows.claim: He attributes the bright faces to the traces of ablution, connected with the well-known report about the luminous marks of washing.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk’ten rivayette “âsâr-ı vuzû’dandır” denilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation attributes the brightness to enduring hardship and dust while striving for a long time in God’s path; the author calls this the most inclusive wording.
rows.anchor: Allah yolunda uzun müddet toz toprakla mücahedeye katlanmaktan

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi explains the brightness as release from the world and arrival at the holy realm and the stations of mercy and divine pleasure.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Bence bu, dünyadan halâs ve âlem-i kudse ve rahmet ü rıdvan menâziline vusul sebebiyledir.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts Razi’s explanation but says the key question is which worldly causes bring about that release and arrival.
rows.anchor: Doğru, lâkin asıl mesele o halâs ve vusûlün dünyadaki esbâbını bilmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radiant faces laugh because they have escaped the reckoning.
rows.anchor: Güler, çünkü hesabdan kurtulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejoice because they receive glad tidings of mercy and divine pleasure and meet God’s beauty.
rows.anchor: Müjdelenir, sevinir çünkü rahmet ü rıdvan ile cemâl-i Hakk’a kavuşmaktadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other faces bear dust and soot-like darkness together, a terrifying manifestation of fear, humiliation, pain, and punishment.
rows.anchor: Yüzlerde böyle tortozla karanın ictimâ‘ı ise havf u zillet ile elem ve azâbın en mûhiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These dark-faced people are disbelievers and wicked sinners who combine unbelief with wrongdoing, which God makes their public disgrace.
rows.anchor: Onlar küfr ile fücûru cem‘etmiş, Allah teâlâ da onu onlara tortoz içinde yüzler karası etmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should prepare before that day by fearing God, avoiding unbelief and sin, obeying, and seeking purification through faith and Islam so they may arrive rejoicing and radiant.
rows.anchor: o gün gelmeden kendi meşiyyet ve iradesiyle bütün bunları düşünüp Allah’tan korkarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present world will not endure; as the next surah says, the sun will be folded and stars will go out, leaving deeds and either radiant faces or disgrace before God.
rows.anchor: Bundan sonraki sûrede geleceği vechile o Güneş dürülüp yıldızlar sönecek

none: The segment gives the verse translation and Arabic text only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As‘asa has opposite senses: the night’s approach and its departure, so the oath’s wording can carry either meaning.
rows.anchor: ezdâddan olmak üzere hem ikbal hem idbar mânalarına geldiği cihetle

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some take the night’s approach as its first hours, when it begins to darken, which carries a warning.
rows.anchor: Gecenin ikbâli vakti, kararmaya başladığı ilk saatleridir

rows.speaker: Ekseriyet
rows.claim: Most commentators prefer the night’s departure, its final hours as it turns toward dawn, heralding the morning.
rows.anchor: İdbârı vakti de zevâle yüz tuttuğu, sabaha yöneldiği son saatleridir

rows.speaker: Buhârî
rows.claim: Bukhari also transmits the departing sense of as‘asa, making the phrase like the oath in 74:33; Elmalılı’s rendering is intended to suggest both senses.
rows.anchor: demiştir ki Sûre-i Müddessir’deki وَالَّيْلِ اِذْ اَدْبَرَ [74/33] gibi olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The morning’s breathing means the moment it starts to brighten, like 74:34, and also evokes the delicacy of the gentle morning breeze.
rows.anchor: gibi açılmaya başladığı sıradır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn dispels the distress of night and promises the Prophet and Muslims a good outcome, as expressed in 93:4.
rows.anchor: mazmûnu üzere hüsn-i âkıbet ile va‘d ü tebşir vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ present world is a night turning toward morning, and the Judgment when each soul learns what it prepared is like a breathing dawn.
rows.anchor: Bu dünya onlar için sabaha yönelmiş bir gece ve her nefsin ne hazırlamış olduğunu bileceği o kıyamet vakti böyle teneffüs eden bir sabah demek olduğunu müjdelemektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths affirm that the Qur’an reporting these events is speech brought by an honored messenger; this messenger is Gabriel, the Trustworthy Spirit.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı Peygamber’e getiren Rûh-ı Emîn Cebrâil aleyhisselâm’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is powerful in carrying out his commission, with strength beyond resistance or doubt, as in 53:5–6.
rows.anchor: Pek kuvvetli hâmil olduğu risâleti, me’mur bulunduğu emri îfâda zaafı yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel has great honor near the Lord of the Throne and is obeyed by the angels there, from whom he receives commands and to whom they refer.
rows.anchor: melâike-i mukarrebîn ona itaat ederler, onun emrini dinlerler. Ondan emir telakkī eder ve ona müracaat eylerler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is utterly trustworthy in revelation and never transgresses what he is commanded to deliver.
rows.anchor: emrolunduğu bir şeyde asla te‘addîsi olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from Gabriel says he never exceeds what he has been commanded to do.
rows.anchor: benim emanetim, ben bir şey ile emrolunayım da onu başkasına tecavüz edeyim, bu vâki‘olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad, addressed as the audience’s companion, is not mad; the companion wording recalls 53:2 and subtly appeals to their years of knowing him, as in 10:16.
rows.anchor: sâhibiniz sohbetinde bulunduğunuz arkadaşınız, yani Hazret-i Peygamber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience knows Muhammad’s sound mind, virtue, and goodwill; he speaks the truth as one confirming God’s messengers, not as a madman.
rows.anchor: Akıl ve idrâki tam, fazl u fazileti müsellem, hakkınızda hayırhah bir zattır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad saw Gabriel in his true form at the clear horizon, the eastern horizon where daylight comes and makes things visible, also called the highest horizon in 53:7.
rows.anchor: gündüzün geldiği, Güneş’in doğduğu, eşyâyı tebyin ettirip gösteren maşrık tarafı diye tefsir edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: One report from Mujahid locates the highest clear horizon near Ajiad, also called Jiyad, a mountain or tract east of Mecca.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den bir rivayette “Ecyad tarafından ufuk-ı mübîn-i a‘lâda” diye vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the highest clear horizon with the head of Cancer, regarded by Meccans as the highest point of rising.
rows.anchor: ehl-i Mekke için metâli‘in en yükseği Seretan burcunun re’s-i matla‘ı olduğundan “ufuk-ı mübîn-i a‘lâ”dan murad odur denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe Gabriel appearing between earth and heaven upon the Kursi in his created form with six hundred wings.
rows.anchor: Arz ve semâ arasında Kürsî üzerinde Allah teâlâ’nın halkeylediği surette gördü, altı yüz cenâhı vardı diye rivayet olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: Âmir
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Jarir says Gabriel appeared once in his own form and otherwise as a man called Dihya; on that occasion he filled the horizon and wore green silk brocade with pearls.
rows.anchor: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Cibrîl’i kendi suretinde bir kere görmüştü. Diğerlerinde Dıhye denilen bir recül suretinde gelirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad certainly saw Gabriel a second time at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, as 53:13–14 states.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın Cibrîl’i sûret-i hakīkiyesiyle Sidre-i Müntehâ’nın yanında bir kere daha görmüş olduğu da muhakkaktır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the vision at this verse with the vision beside the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan buradaki rü’yetin Sidre-i Müntehâ yanındaki rü’yet olduğu da rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because 53:13–14 distinguishes the later vision from the highest-horizon sight, the author takes the clear horizon broadly enough to encompass both reports; Gabriel was seen in his true form twice.
rows.anchor: ufuk-ı mübîn, ufuk-ı a‘lâ ile Sidre-i Müntehâ’dan e‘am mülâhaza edilmek daha muvâfık olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Danin derives from dann, stinginess, and may be active or passive: the Prophet neither withholds revelation nor is someone to be envied for receiving it.
rows.anchor: “Danîn” buhl demek olan “dann”dan fe‘îldir. Fâil mânasına da mef‘ul mânasına da olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the active reading, the Prophet freely conveys revelation and unseen matters instead of withholding knowledge for payment, so self-interest is no plausible accusation.
rows.anchor: Almış olduğu vahyi tebliğ etmekte ve sizin müşahedenizden ve ilminizden gāib bulunan bilmediğiniz şeyleri haber verip bildirmekte bahillik etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the passive reading, it is unsurprising that a man of Muhammad’s known intellect and virtue receives revelation; God’s choice of him is no cause for envy, as in 10:2.
rows.anchor: Onun gaybdan haber vermesi, vahiy alması, sizin bilmediğiniz şeyleri bilmesi çok görülmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readings use zanin with ظ, interpreted either as not suspect but trustworthy, or as not weak in capacity, memory, or transmission.
rows.anchor: Bu da iki mâna ile tefsir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second zanin sense rejects any notion that the Prophet speaks from weakness, poor memory, conjecture, or passion; he receives and conveys revelation with certainty without losing a letter.
rows.anchor: O kuvvetli, emîn Resûl-i Kerîm’den tam bir müşahede üzerine aldığı teblîğātı tam bir kuvvet ile alıp hıfzederek hiçbir harfini zâyi‘etmeksizin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is delivered with strength and trust from the honored messenger, leaving no doubt that God, the Lord of the Throne, sent it.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın göndermiş olduğunda hiç[^18] şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is not the speech of a banished devil; Gabriel is an honored, obedient messenger, unlike demons who steal hearing and are pelted, as in 37:8–9.
rows.anchor: kâhinlere görünenler gibi Mele-i A‘lâ’dan kulak hırsızlığı edip de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the messenger seen by Muhammad and Muhammad himself are far removed from Satan and satanic influence.
rows.anchor: onu gören ve size haber veren sâhibiniz de şeytan ve şeytanetten uzaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks why the audience abandons the straight path and falls into grave error despite these truths.
rows.anchor: Bu hakikatlere karşı doğru yolu bırakıp da nelere zâhib oluyor, ne büyük dalâletlere düşüyorsunuz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a pure reminder for rational beings, especially those who choose uprightness, because they benefit from admonition; guiding such seekers is its purpose.
rows.anchor: bilhassa içinizden müstakīm olmak, hakk u savâbı arayarak doğru gitmek dileyenler için çünkü tezkirden, va‘z u nasihatten menfaat görecek olanlar onlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who refuse uprightness do not benefit; they distort the reminder and increase their loss, as in 17:82.
rows.anchor: gafletlerinden uyandırmaz, uyandırsa da onlar, eğrilikten hoşlandıkları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accountability applies to voluntary acts: people must first direct thought toward truth and resolve toward good, though human willing is not by itself a sufficient or independent cause of success.
rows.anchor: Demek ki teklif ve mes’ûliyet ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyeye aittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context addresses all people, especially those who seek uprightness: their willing depends on God willing their will, so success must be credited to divine grace rather than human independence.
rows.anchor: Siz o istikāmeti başka bir sebep ve suretle dilemiyorsunuz, ancak Allah’ın onu meşiyyetiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading makes the audience those unwilling to be upright and takes God’s willing as coercion; the author rejects this as contrary to the preceding address to uprightness-seekers and sees it as a Mu‘tazilite argument for human independence.
rows.anchor: İnsanı meşiyyetinde tamamen müstakil ve fiilinin hâlıkı addetmek isteyen Mutezile bu mânaya sarılmak istemişlerse de

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud gives a finer sense: humans cannot will with a will that entails uprightness unless God wills that will.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ أَيِ الإِْسْتِقَامَةَ مَشِيَّةً مُسْتَتْبِعَةً لَهَا demekle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God willing a servant’s willing does not guarantee the servant’s intended result: people may want the right path but stumble; if God willed the result, it would occur.
rows.anchor: Allah abdin iradesini irade etmekle murâdını da irade etmiş olmak lâzım gelmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the person’s will and its realization require conjunction with God’s will; a barren will that does not lead to uprightness cannot be the favor meant here.
rows.anchor: abdin hem iradesi hem murâdı husûle gelmek için ikisinin de Allah’ın iradesine iktirânı şart olduğunu anlatmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object after God’s willing is understood from context as the human will, while the object of human willing is uprightness; this contextual reading best fits the passage.
rows.anchor: mâna اِلاَّ اَنْ يَشَاءَ اللّٰهُ مشيتكم demek olduğu şüphesizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some prefer a universal maxim: no human will of any kind exists without God’s will, an explicit Sunni reading; the author says it is less connected to the passage’s focus on uprightness.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın meşiyyeti olmadıkça abdin hiçbir meşiyyeti olamayacağı sarâhaten ve bi’l-ibâre ifade edilmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not erase human willing in favor of absolute compulsion; it negates only willing detached from God’s will and affirms human willing under divine will, an intermediate compulsion.
rows.anchor: burada abdin meşiyyeti külliyen nefyedilmiş değil, meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeye iktiran etmeyen meşiyyeti selbedilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Maturidi position treats universal capacity as created but partial human will as a relational matter needing no separate maker; it permits human choice while keeping all events within God’s will.
rows.anchor: Mâturîdiyye mezhebi bu esas üzerindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is neither absolute compulsion nor absolute delegation; God creates and commands, and nothing occurs outside the Lord of the worlds’ will, as in 28:68 and 7:54.
rows.anchor: Onun için ibâdın ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyesinde ne cebr-i mahz ne de tefvîz-i mahz yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must seek truth by choosing uprightness, credit success to God, remember that God can withdraw the will granted, and not assume every personal wish is right.
rows.anchor: insanlar istikāmeti dileyerek hakk u savâbı aramalı ve o suretle bu zikirden istifade etmelidir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Cehil
rows.claim: A report says Abu Jahl took the uprightness verse to mean people were left to choose for themselves; then the verse about God’s will was revealed.
rows.anchor: Ebû Cehil “demek ki iş bize bırakılmıştır[^30], dilersek müstakīm oluruz, dilersek olmayız” demişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that report, the verse counters pure delegation and urges people to seek uprightness from God; its warning and reference to compelling divine will are indirect.
rows.anchor: bu âyet, cebri isbat için değil, tefvîz-i mahzı nefy ile istikāmeti Allah’tan dilemeye teşvik siyâkında nâzil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s splitting is the appearance and realization of the divine command from above that transforms the present world; it begins with splitting and ends with folding, then creation is renewed as in 21:104.
rows.anchor: bu âlemin tebeddülü için fevkinden gelen emr-i ilâhînin nüzul ve tahakkuk etmek üzere semâda zuhurudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The splitting is at once the destruction of the present heaven and the establishment of the next heaven.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle inşikāk bir taraftan dünya semâsının yıkımı diğer taraftan uhrâ semâsının kuruluşudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first stage is the sky splitting with clouds and angels descending progressively, signaling the arrival of the divine command; judgment’s completion is described in 2:210.
rows.anchor: semânın gamâm ile yarılışı ve melâikenin peyderpey indirilişi ve bu suretle emr-i ilâhînin gelmeye başlayışı

rows.speaker: Şihâb
rows.claim: He explains the clouds as a mist arising during the split, containing the records of deeds and angels as they descend.
rows.anchor: Şihâb’ın beyânına göre inşikāk sırasında hâdis olup içinde suhuf-ı a‘mâl ile melâike inecek olan bir dabâb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the sky was first created from smoke, an explosion in a celestial body could by God’s command produce a cloud and a rupture in some region of heaven.
rows.anchor: Semâ bidâyeten bir duhan olarak yaratıldığı gibi semânın herhangi bir tarafında ecrâmın birinde bi-emrillah vâki‘olacak bir infilâktan

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Shihab’s gloss in the Qadi commentary reports Ibn Abbas interpreting the verse through the sky splitting with clouds in 25:25; absent that report, Shihab would prefer leaving that specification aside.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan me’surdur[^3]. Bu olmasaydı burada onu terketmek evlâ olurdu.

rows.speaker: Şihâb
rows.claim: Shihab says the inchoative form inshaqqat conveys perfect divine power and the sky’s submission without needing an agent to split it.
rows.anchor: inşikākın ihtiyar olunmasında kemâl-i kudrete ve sanki şakka ihtiyaç yokmuş gibi inkiyâda delâlet eden bir mâna vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj says the sky will split from the terror of resurrection and become fragile, as in 69:16; this need not conflict with a cloud accompanying it.
rows.anchor: bunun gamâm ile olmasına münâfî olmayacağı da söylenmiştir.

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report from Ali says the splitting will begin at the Milky Way; some traditions call the Milky Way the sky’s door, and astronomers identify it as many indistinguishable stars.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den bir rivayette bu inşikākın mecerreden olacağı da mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Milky Way’s nature was recognized by earlier and modern astronomers, not newly discovered by telescopes; its high, distant location suggests a rupture beginning from above.
rows.anchor: Mecerrelerin seçilemeyen birçok yıldızlar mecmû‘ası olduğunda eski ve yeni hey’etçilerin ittifâkı var demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s splitting unfolds in stages from its beginning through its final folding and judgment, as described across 25:25, 55:37, 69:16, and 78:19.
rows.anchor: Böyle bir infitâr ile başlayacak olan inşikāk-ı semânın nihâyet tayy ve kazâ-i emre kadar gittikçe inkişaf eden birtakım safahâtı vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two idha clauses group the sky’s three events under one time and the earth’s events under another, covering the related stages of each.
rows.anchor: semâya ait انْشَقَّتْ، وَاَذِنَتْ، وَحُقَّتْ fiillerinin mecmû‘u bir اِذَا, Arz’a ait olanlar da bir اِذَا tahtında cem‘olunarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky listening to its Lord is a metaphor: paying heed means obeying and submitting to the divine command.
rows.anchor: kulak vermek, dinlemek mânasından olarak inkiyad ve itaatte mecazdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s line uses adhinū for listening: people are deaf when they hear good spoken of the poet but listen when someone mentions evil.
rows.anchor: Benim anıldığım bir hayr işittiklerinde sağırdırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At creation, heaven and earth obeyed the command to come willingly or unwillingly and answered that they came obediently; likewise the sky submits to the later command without resistance.
rows.anchor: diye tav‘an ona inkıyad edip bütün tabiatlarıyla vücûda geldikleri gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huqqat can mean the sky was made worthy by its nature to listen and obey, or that obedience was made obligatory; if it did not obey willingly it would be compelled.
rows.anchor: Biri liyâkatten, biri vücubdan olan bu iki mânaca وَحُقَّتْ’de vâv âtıfe olmayıp cümle-i mu‘teriza

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss says heaven was made deserving of listening and submission, unable to resist; another says God imposed obedience on it, while a further gloss makes splitting obligatory because of the terror’s intensity.
rows.anchor: semâ dinleyip inkıyad etmeye, imtinâ‘etmemeye şâyan kılınmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads listening broadly as obedience not only to the split but also to ensuing commands, such as angels descending; huqqat then signals the inevitable Event or the triumph of truth, as in 2:210, 69:17, and 89:22.
rows.anchor: yalnız inşikāk emrini değil, onunla beraber melâikenin nüzûlü ve daha sâir ahkâm-ı rabbâniyenin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is spread either by leveling mountains and valleys into a flat plain, as in 20:106–107, or by being drawn out and made wider.
rows.anchor: Ve Arz meddolunduğu dağları dereleri dekk ile tesviye edilip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth casts out what it contains: the dead from their graves and its hidden weights, treasures, and minerals, as in 99:2.
rows.anchor: ve içinde ne varsa attığı ölüleri kabirlerinden fırlattığı

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Some, including Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, restrict the earth’s expelled contents to the dead because treasures are released at the Antichrist’s emergence; the author favors the broader account attributed to Qatadah.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr gibi birtakımları künûzün ihrâcı Deccâl’in hurûcu sırasında olduğuna binâen burada yalnız mevtâya kasretmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says the earth will open first for the Prophet; after he sits in his grave and asks why it moves, the earth says its Lord ordered it to cast out what it held and empty itself as before creation.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer radıyallahu anh’tan tahric etmiştir ki Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem şöyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s emptying and listening to its Lord follow the same explanation as the sky; repeating idha distinguishes the two phases and their respective subjects.
rows.anchor: semâya ait olanlarla Arz’a ait olanların bir nevi hususiyetle istiklâline

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ on the idha clauses: they may be adverbial without an answer, answer an implied question about recompense, omit an answer for awe, mean everyone learns their deeds, or contain their answer in the obedience verbs.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu اِذَا’ların şart mânasından mücerred zarfiyye olup cevâba muhtaç olmadığını söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best answer to the clauses is found in one of the following two verses.
rows.anchor: Fakat en doğrusu cevap şu iki âyetten birinin mazmûnundadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kedh means scratching or exerting serious effort in good or evil; throughout life and after death people strive toward an outcome from their Lord, painful or pleasant.
rows.anchor: tırmalamak ve kendisine tesir edecek vechile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take famulaqihi as the answer to the idha clauses, while others make verse 6 itself the answer; the author prefers treating verse 6 as parenthetical and verse 7 as the answer.
rows.anchor: Fakat en doğrusu cevap şu iki âyetten birinin mazmûnundadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given their record, or its announcement, in the right hand receive an easy reckoning, with the related discussion in Surah al-Haqqa.
rows.anchor: defter-i a‘mâli veya i‘lâmı sağ eliyle veya sağ eline verilen (Sûre-i Hâkka’ya bak)
